focus.claude: SELF-CORRECTION. Does the network notice its own wrong steps? Build matched pairs from practice traces: a clean reasoning prefix, and the same prefix with ONE step corrupted (a number, sign, unit or negation changed so the step is false). In teacher-forced read passes, measure what follows the corrupted step vs the clean one: P of re-check tokens ('Wait', 'Actually', 'Let me double-check'), and residual-stream directions that separate corrupted from clean at the step end (fit on some pairs, test on held-out pairs). Then ask whether the signal REACHES the behaviour: in the parent's own wrong traces (pass@4 bank), is the error signal present at the first wrong step but not followed by a re-check? If there is a real detector whose link to re-checking is weak, strengthen that link (only when the detector fires; raising re-checking everywhere is a global knob and out of scope) and show on held-out corrupted pairs that detection->re-check rises while clean steps are left alone. Then test generated conclusions on mixed pass@4 questions. If the network has no error signal, say so clearly: that is an important negative result.
focus.ed_f: STEP-LEVEL REASONING ERRORS. Use the pass@4 bank at 8,192 (same question, right and wrong samples). For each finished WRONG sample of a mixed question, find the FIRST false step and classify it (false fact recalled; arithmetic/algebra slip; number or condition copied wrongly from the question; NOT/EXCEPT/units/sign lost; formula or definition misapplied; unsupported leap), and note what the right samples did at the same point. Check that the most frequent class holds on a larger set before spending passes on it (your gen-12 diagnosis did not replicate at 256 questions). Pick the class that is most frequent AND has a findable cause; localise the cause with teacher-forced read passes (e.g. at the error token: which heads attend to the source in the question, which MLP neurons write the wrong value; compare with right samples at the same point), edit it, and show on held-out texts that P(correct step) rises relative to P(wrong step) before you generate. Arithmetic or copying slips are a good place to start if they are frequent, because they also matter for GSM8K.
